WhoNext 1.0 (063)

  • New opt-in, encrypted direct support access to saved meetings, notes, transcripts, processing jobs, logs and retained recordings. Pair the development Mac once; direct reads do not depend on iCloud.
  • One calm meeting window from Stop through three processing stages to the saved note, with background continuation and recovery.
  • Rename speakers throughout linked note references and transcript labels without another AI call. Consolidate duplicate speakers with confirmation and Undo while preserving acoustic evidence and manual edits.
  • Name and consolidate observed voices during recording, with stable anonymous labels, freshness-aware activity and evidence-backed final speaker mapping.
  • Improved relationship naming, factual-correction admission and explicit uncertainty for suspected microphone echo. The iCloud fallback now distinguishes local publication from confirmed delivery.

Manual-validation release: 702 tests passed, zero failed, 22 opt-in tests skipped. Direct-support checks include native Keychain pairing/revocation, authenticated TLS, wrong-key rejection, saved 1:1/group reads and bounded recording downloads. The family-audio repair worklist and complete long/four-hour paced, hardware and accessibility matrix remain outstanding; these are not certified by the unit suite.

Direct access needs one-time enablement/pairing and a reachable LAN or private network. It is read-only and provides no shell access or Internet relay. Requires macOS 26.0 or later, Apple silicon. Built with Xcode 27 beta on macOS 27 beta; the owner will validate the Studio installation.

WhoNext 1.0 (062)

  • Verified local microphone speech uses your configured name without requiring a calendar entry or AI identity guess. This fixes a validation conflict that could discard otherwise complete meeting notes.
  • Failed recorded meetings remain in the recording recovery flow with Retry, instead of asking for an external transcript to be pasted.
  • Speaker inference receives measured turn ends when available and distinguishes overlapping speech from a reply to a named person.
  • Local identity survives note rendering and action ownership. Repeated Retry actions save a completed note only once.
  • Capture-publication timeouts use an absolute monotonic deadline.

Manual-validation release: three independent serial test runs each passed 625 tests, with 20 opt-in skips. Fresh full-transcript note replays completed in approximately 163 seconds for a 15-minute meeting and 107 seconds for an hour-long meeting. These are note-generation timings, not new capture-to-note measurements. Parallel stress timing failures and the wider long-recording matrix remain outstanding.

Published at the owner's request for manual Teams testing on the Mac Studio. Requires macOS 26.0 or later, Apple silicon. Built with Xcode 27 beta on macOS 27 beta; macOS 26 runtime and the final hardware capture test remain unverified.

WhoNext 1.0 (061)

  • Meeting notes show supported names normally, without an “AI-identified” suffix. Confidence and confirmation status remain intact internally.
  • Improved whole-conversation identity review uses introductions, named handoffs and corroborating evidence across turns. Human corrections remain authoritative.
  • Improved frame-aligned echo processing, reusable transcription checkpoints and independent capture shutdown reduce work after Stop and improve recovery.
  • Private incremental preparation supports final analysis without replacing the complete transcript. Claude and ChatGPT/Codex subscription processing remains.
  • Expanded diagnostics and isolated replay tooling help investigate failures using retained recordings.

Manual-validation release: recent hour-long paced recording tests saved notes within five minutes of Stop; these predate the final attribution/display changes. A subsequent full-transcript notes-only replay resolved previously unnamed presenters. Wider long-meeting, labelled accuracy and real Teams hardware checks remain incomplete. Some speech gaps and acoustic speaker assignments still need attention; five minutes is not yet a universal guarantee.

Requires macOS 26.0 or later. Built on macOS 27 beta with Xcode 27 beta. This update is being released at the owner's request for real-world testing.

WhoNext 1.0 (060)

Whole-transcript Claude analysis, with one ChatGPT/Codex fallback, and corrections to recording, transcription timing and recovery.

  • Claude receives the complete conversation and participant context together, producing a comprehensive note and evidence-backed speaker proposals. Automatic local Qwen notes and routine multi-stage note synthesis are removed from this path.
  • Stop drains accepted audio before files close. Durable job claims, fenced checkpoints and reusable transcription chunks reduce duplicate work and allow interrupted processing to resume.
  • Apple/Whisper routing is consistent; confidence checks are engine-specific. Partial word alignment preserves text and marks timing uncertainty. System-audio offsets are corrected.
  • Names can use cross-speaker introduction and substitute evidence. Actions distinguish requester, proposed owner and accepted commitment. Unresolved voices retain stable speaker labels.
  • Settings expose separate Claude and ChatGPT/Codex status, sign-in and refresh actions. O365 remains separately connected; missing calendar access does not prevent notes.
  • Provider process cleanup is bounded; a complete note must validate before acceptance. Five minutes is a progress milestone, not a whole-meeting cancellation timer.

Manual-validation release: 476 local tests passed, 3 were skipped, and none failed. Retained-meeting replays, the 90-minute production run, real-provider end-to-end checks and the Teams smoke test remain pending. Real-meeting accuracy and latency are not yet certified.

Requires macOS 26.0 or later. Built with Xcode 27 beta. After updating, check Claude, ChatGPT/Codex and O365 connection status in Settings before testing.
